items.stem: The same two courses are written as JSON, XML and HTML. Which format is the largest, and why?

options.text: HTML, because it also carries layout such as table widths
options.feedback: HTML describes how to draw the table, so only 13% of its bytes are the data. JSON is the smallest.

options.text: XML, because every single value is wrapped in tags
options.feedback: XML is larger than JSON, but HTML adds layout on top of its tags, so it is larger still.

options.text: JSON, because it is the newest of the three formats
options.feedback: JSON is the smallest of the three, because it has the least packaging around the values.

items.try: In the step "Compare data formats", select each format and compare the three bars.

items.stem: A university news site shows articles. Most visitors read one article and leave. Which way of building pages fits this best?

options.text: Server-rendered pages, because the first screen arrives ready to draw
options.feedback: A single-page app must download a large bundle before showing anything. That cost pays off only over many pages.

options.text: A single-page app, because it moves less data over many page views
options.feedback: It moves less data only after many page views. A visitor who views one page pays for the whole bundle and gets nothing back.

options.text: Either one, because both send the same amount of data to the visitor
options.feedback: The amounts differ. A single-page app sends the 280 KB bundle first, while a server-rendered page sends about 45 KB.

items.stem: Staff keep an internal tool open all day and click through hundreds of screens. Which model moves less data over a day?

options.text: A single-page app, because each click fetches only a few KB of JSON
options.feedback: The bundle is downloaded once. Every later click moves much less data than a full HTML page.

options.text: Server-rendered pages, because they never have to download a bundle
options.feedback: Each click sends a full page of about 45 KB. Over hundreds of clicks that adds up to far more than the bundle.

options.text: Both move the same amount, because the data in each page is the same
options.feedback: The data is the same, but the packaging is not. A full page repeats layout on every click.
